steps.title: Name the filled shape code
steps.instruction: Replace the tested example with this function and its call. Keep the call at the left edge.
steps.explain: def polygon(points, c) names the code you tested. Its inputs replace the fixed values. The call underneath supplies those values and runs the indented body.
steps.expected: The practice shape should still appear. This step includes both the definition and a call.

steps.title: Place four oval points
steps.instruction: Start with the right, top, left, and bottom points. Join them with your polygon function.
steps.explain: An oval has a horizontal radius and a vertical radius. These four points show its width and height before we add points between them.
steps.expected: A diamond occupying the oval’s width and height. It is a rough first outline.
steps.question: Which pair of points controls the width?
steps.answer: The left and right points. Their x-coordinates are the center minus or plus the horizontal radius.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Add points between the corners
steps.instruction: Replace the four fixed points with a loop that calculates twelve positions.
steps.explain: math.cos(angle) and math.sin(angle) give the horizontal and vertical parts of a position around a circle. Multiplying them by different radii stretches the shape. points.append() saves each calculated pair.
steps.expected: A twelve-sided outline with the same width and height. The corners now look rounder.
steps.question: What would happen if the horizontal and vertical radii were equal?
steps.answer: The points would form a circle.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Smooth the oval
steps.instruction: Increase the sample count from 12 to 48 in both places.
steps.explain: More points make shorter straight segments. The full turn still covers 2 × pi radians, so the shape keeps the same size.
steps.expected: A smooth oval in the same position.
steps.question: Why change the divisor as well as the range?
steps.answer: The angle spacing must match the number of segments so the points cover exactly one full turn.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Name the tested oval code
steps.instruction: Put the working calculation in a function. Supply its position, two radii, and color in the call.
steps.explain: The function uses the same point calculation. x and y move the center; rx and ry control the two radii; c supplies the color.
steps.expected: The same oval, now drawn with one call.
steps.question: Which input would make the oval taller without making it wider?
steps.answer: ry, the vertical radius.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

lines: def oval(x, y, rx, ry, c):
points.append((x + rx * math.cos(angle), y + ry * math.sin(angle)))
